# TEST-RECORD.md — full test-suite output

A verbatim record of the suite, re-verified after every phase gate.
Generated from a real run, not transcribed by hand. This file is a snapshot: it is
**not** regenerated by `npm run check`, so if the code changes it goes stale — rerun
the commands in [§4](#4-how-this-was-produced) to refresh it.

### `tests/finance.golden.test.ts` — 44 passed

**the EMI formula itself**

- ✓ matches the hand-computed base EMI to the paisa
- ✓ returns P/n at a zero rate, with no division by zero
- ✓ returns zero for a zero principal rather than NaN
- ✓ rejects inputs that cannot produce a schedule

**the amortisation base — the one place the three treatments differ**

- ✓ grows the principal by (1+r)^m under CAPITALISED
- ✓ leaves the principal untouched under SERVICED and WAIVED
- ✓ collapses to the plain principal when there is no moratorium

**moratorium interest**

- ✓ is P·((1+r)^m − 1) under CAPITALISED
- ✓ is exactly P·r·m under SERVICED
- ✓ is zero under WAIVED

**ROADMAP Appendix A — the three treatments end to end**

- ✓ CAPITALISED: EMI ₹2,110.11 and total outflow ₹1,26,606.53
- ✓ SERVICED: EMI ₹2,027.64, outflow ₹1,25,658.37, ₹666.67 paid monthly during the moratorium
- ✓ WAIVED: EMI ₹2,027.64 and total outflow ₹1,21,658.37

**the three Appendix A invariants — the ones implementations get wrong**

- ✓ 1. CAPITALISED EMI is strictly higher than the other two
- ✓ 2. SERVICED and WAIVED share an EMI and differ in outflow by exactly P·r·m
- ✓ 3. a zero rate gives EMI = P/n across all three treatments

**the schedule always adds up — hard rule 7 > CAPITALISED**

- ✓ has one row per month, moratorium included
- ✓ closes at exactly zero
- ✓ never lets the balance go negative mid-schedule
- ✓ repays exactly the amortised principal
- ✓ has rounded totals that equal the sum of the rounded rows
- ✓ accounts for the moratorium in exactly one of the two moratorium totals
- ✓ has rounded totals within a rupee per instalment of the exact ones

**the schedule always adds up — hard rule 7 > SERVICED**

- ✓ has one row per month, moratorium included
- ✓ closes at exactly zero
- ✓ never lets the balance go negative mid-schedule
- ✓ repays exactly the amortised principal
- ✓ has rounded totals that equal the sum of the rounded rows
- ✓ accounts for the moratorium in exactly one of the two moratorium totals
- ✓ has rounded totals within a rupee per instalment of the exact ones

**the schedule always adds up — hard rule 7 > WAIVED**

- ✓ has one row per month, moratorium included
- ✓ closes at exactly zero
- ✓ never lets the balance go negative mid-schedule
- ✓ repays exactly the amortised principal
- ✓ has rounded totals that equal the sum of the rounded rows
- ✓ accounts for the moratorium in exactly one of the two moratorium totals
- ✓ has rounded totals within a rupee per instalment of the exact ones

**edge shapes that must not throw**

- ✓ handles a zero-month moratorium
- ✓ handles a single repayment instalment
- ✓ rejects a fractional or zero repayment term

**the rounding policy**

- ✓ is half-up, not banker’s
- ✓ normalises negative zero
- ✓ throws on non-finite input rather than propagating NaN into a schedule
- ✓ does not round rates

### `tests/loan.test.ts` — 33 passed

**the pipeline, step by step**

- ✓ caps the project at the unit cost, subsidises, takes the margin, then caps the loan
- ✓ never raises the project to the ceiling
- ✓ subtracts a FRONT subsidy from the loan and a BACK subsidy from nothing
- ✓ reports MAX_LOAN when the scheme ceiling on the loan is what binds
- ✓ reports GROSS when several constraints bind at once, as the more informative answer
- ✓ floors the loan at zero rather than going negative on a 100% margin
- ✓ flags a loan below the scheme minimum instead of quietly dropping it

**the cost ceiling can be purpose-specific**

- ✓ uses the purpose rule and says so
- ✓ falls back to the scheme scalar for a purpose with no rule
- ✓ takes only the fields the rule states, leaving max_loan to the scheme

**the rate comes from the table, never from a default**

- ✓ picks the band the sanctioned loan falls into
- ✓ prefers the more specific rule when two apply
- ✓ refuses to price when no rule matches the loan band
- ✓ refuses to price when the matched rule has no rate yet
- ✓ carries the rate’s provenance onto the result, so the UI can badge it

**terms — the ROADMAP §8.1 open question, made visible**

- ✓ subtracts the moratorium from the tenure when the tenure includes it
- ✓ adds the moratorium to the tenure when the tenure excludes it
- ✓ refuses to guess when the scheme does not say which reading applies
- ✓ reports a contradiction that leaves no instalments as a diagnostic, not a crash
- ✓ clamps the requested moratorium into the scheme’s range
- ✓ falls back to the scheme pre-fill, then to the minimum, when nothing is requested
- ✓ honours a requested tenure shorter than the scheme maximum

**the moratorium treatment is a scheme field, and it changes the money**

- ✓ produces a higher EMI when interest is capitalised than when it is waived
- ✓ delegates entirely to amortise() rather than doing its own arithmetic

**refusing to compute — the branch no persona reaches**

- ✓ reports every gap in one pass, not the first one it hits
- ✓ does not repeat a path
- ✓ names every gap in a way the UI can render — hard rule 3
- ✓ demands the subsidy cap and timing only when a subsidy actually exists
- ✓ carries no figures at all on the refusing branch

**rounding and reconciliation**

- ✓ reports whole rupees that add up on screen
- ✓ does not round the rate

**purity**

- ✓ returns a deeply equal result for the same input twice
- ✓ mutates neither the scheme nor the applicant

## 3. The one deliberate gap

`tests/finance.golden.test.ts` ends with a `describe.todo(...)` block holding no test
cases. That is intentional and must stay empty until real scheme parameters exist:
writing those cases requires published figures for margin, subsidy, ceiling, rate,
tenure and moratorium treatment, and filling them in from plausible-looking numbers
would make the suite assert invented values. `describe.todo` registers no cases, which
is why the counts in §1 are unaffected by it.

The gap is a missing *dataset*, not missing *coverage*: the engine itself is covered by
the 44 passing tests above, which pin the formula, all three moratorium treatments and
the rounding policy against hand-computed values.
